completion_data.completion_summary: Resolved the reviser-agent handoff-writer contract contradiction: added an orchestrator_mode-gated .orchestrator-handoff.json section to agents/reviser-agent.md, registered it in docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md's Handoff Writers table, added a clarifying note to skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's Skill-to-Agent Mapping table, and corrected a stale comment in scripts/reconcile-task-status.sh. Also bumped orchestrator-context-budget.json's SKILL.md ceiling (24500 -> 25000 B) to keep Gate 20 green after the required clarifying note.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's TARGET positional argument must be a repo root (it checks TARGET/.claude and TARGET/agent-system/extensions to classify source-store vs. deploy-consumer), never an extension subdirectory like agent-system/extensions/core. Passing the extension path as TARGET exits 2 with 'no deploy tree at <path>/.claude' instead of running the requested gates. When a plan's verification line names an explicit extension-path TARGET for verify-deploy.sh, omit TARGET (it defaults to $(pwd)) and run from the repo root instead.

lint-agent-contracts.sh Check J (the handoff-writing-section scanner) is content-gated, not list-gated: it only bounds a section in an agent file that already mentions '.orchestrator-handoff.json' somewhere. Adding a new handoff-writing section to a previously handoff-silent agent file automatically brings it under Check J with no lint-script edit required. The inverse gap is real too: a file that later loses every mention of the filename is silently skipped, not failed, so no lint catches a regression that deletes the whole section.

When an edit to commands/orchestrate.md or skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md breaches Gate 20's per-file byte ceiling (orchestrator-context-budget.json), first try folding the new content into an existing table cell/row as a short parenthetical rather than a new paragraph -- this repo's own budget file's dated derivation history shows repeated cases where that alone saved 80%+ of the naive addition's bytes. If a residual overage remains after that compaction, this repo's established, accepted convention is a dated ceiling_bytes bump rounded up to the next 500 B, with a derivation entry describing what was added and what compaction was tried -- not a blocked gate.
